newsitem.title: ITALY: Olivetti firms in Milan in active buying.
newsitem.headline: Olivetti firms in Milan in active buying.

text.p: Shares in Italian information technology group Olivetti rose strongly in heavy volume on a fairly quiet Milan stock market on renewed domestic and foreign buying on expectations of a sale of its ailing PC business, dealers said.
At 1100 GMT, Olivetti was 3.5 percent up at 553 lire, after a high of 558, in volume of over 15 million shares against total volume on Thursday of some 6.0 million.
The all-share Mibtel index posted a 0.32 percent gain.

Olivetti chief executive Roberto Colaninno had said he hoped to sell off the group's loss-making personal computer company by the end of 1996, but in late November he said the process had been delayed.
Some traders said they were perplexed by the frequent speculative spurts in Olivetti stock which were not backed by any concrete facts. "We want to see the deal done, black on white," one said.
